q1_sourceVersionZodType.reasoning: Every minting path yields a positive integer and every other path copies; legacy projections omit the field. The type says number, but the pack already constrains beyond its types where the domain is integral (CampaignDayAdvanced.newDay and CampaignSnapshotPublished.revision are .int()). A value of 0, a negative, a fraction, a string or null is not something production writes, and the event-store requirement says an ill-typed field SHALL fail validation. No server-side schema constrains the unit on the record PUT path (src/lib/scenarioPacks/packSchemas.ts:144-147 validates units as z.array(z.unknown())), so the pack is where a non-production value is refused.
q1_sourceVersionZodType.nonClaim: A record written by a non-UI client could hold any JSON number; the pack would refuse a non-positive or fractional one. No such writer was found.

facts: The fingerprint hashes {eventType, targetSchemaVersion, schemaId} and transition ids only (ReplayPipelineFingerprint.ts:96-114); changing a shape under the same id leaves it unchanged.

The spec (openspec/specs/event-store/spec.md:398-401, "Upcast pipeline changes without a projector change") says: WHEN a target schema changes while the projector stays, the prior checkpoint fingerprint SHALL no longer be compatible. Adding an optional field to a strict target schema is a target-schema change, so keeping the id would leave a changed target under an unchanged fingerprint.

What stores the campaign fingerprint in production: every cutover marker (campaignAuthorityMigration.ts:142), persisted as JSON (CampaignMigrationMarkerStore.ts:59-68). Marker writers run only when isCampaignJournalAuthorityEnabled() is true, which production never is (JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:86; campaignJournalAuthorityEnabled.ts:36-38); markers exist in e2e-armed and development databases.

What compares it: nothing in production. The only comparator, isMaterializedSnapshotCompatible (campaignAuthorityMigration.ts:366-377), has no production caller. No campaign replay checkpoint exists: campaign recovery uses referenceRecoveryPort (campaignEventLog.ts:52-55, CampaignMatchHost.ts:149). The composed replay surfaces fingerprint only the combat types they encounter (ReplaySurfaceGate.ts:131-157), so campaign ids never reach them.

Premise check on option (a): the pack (6cee9c09b, #1258) was committed 2026-08-20; ICampaignRosterUnit.sourceVersion and both producers' sourceVersion writes arrived 2026-08-22 (20f66e145, #1321). Production has therefore NOT written sourceVersion since before the pack existed; the pack predates the field by two days.

options.consequence: fingerprint unchanged; stored markers stay equal; no id or test changes. The target schema of three types changes under an unchanged fingerprint, contrary to the spec scenario's SHALL; the argument that this is a correction rather than a schema change rests on a premise the git history contradicts (the field post-dates the pack). Safe in effect today only because the change is a pure widening (every payload the old schema accepted parses identically under the new one) and no campaign checkpoint exists.

options.summary: revise the schema id of the three types that nest the roster unit (campaign.<type>.v1 -> campaign.<type>.v1-r2) at the same schemaVersion 1; the other five keep campaign.<type>.v1
options.consequence: the fingerprint of any history holding RosterUnitChanged, SalvageAllocated or CampaignSnapshotPublished changes, so a checkpoint or materialization fingerprinted before the change is incompatible and is rebuilt from full replay (the spec law); histories without those types keep their fingerprint (unused registrations do not participate, archived task 1B.2). campaignSchemaPipelineFingerprint() changes, so every stored marker's schemaPipelineFingerprint differs from the live value; nothing compares them today. No pinned test value changes (no literal campaign fingerprint is pinned anywhere; campaignAuthorityMigration.test.ts compares against the computed value). Stored rows keep eventVersion 1 and parse under the revised v1 schema. Matches the modelled "target schema change" at ReplayCheckpointCompatibility.test.ts:256-277.

q3_fingerprintLaw.recommendationReason: It is the only option that satisfies the spec scenario literally (a changed target schema changes the fingerprint) and fixes the refusal, and it needs no file outside the three ownership paths. Its only production-visible consequence, stale marker fingerprints, has no reader today and is the intended D10 behaviour for a future reader. It is scoped to the three affected types, so unaffected histories keep their fingerprint.
